story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: In which direction shall we go Helen? You direct us, tell us what to do.
Well I think we're about to go out. (LAUGHTER).
Maybe in the direction of Long Island. (LAUGHTER).

But I must say this has been a most pleasant afternoon talking with you and reminiscing about things. And I'm certainly happy about the young musicians today. They've got a chance to study and they go to schools and study their instruments and really get a thorough knowledge of their harmonies and everything.
And not be little bums like you were?
That's right. (LAUGHTER). That's right. That's right. But when I took up music boy, I stopped being a bum. I had to devote all my time to that horn.
I really think if you hadn't played music you probably would have wound up being arrested or something.
Well I definitely would because I was on my way. I was a little, a little, you know.
He said he was a little toughie. Little gang. Yes.
Teenage toughie alright.
Speaking of this business of the young musicians. I was quite surprised to find that Southern University in Baton Rouge actually offers a Bachelors Degree in jazz.
where Batiste is?

Yes, he sends his people, yes.
Oh yes, well that's marvellous. There should be more places like that.
Well there should be because this is America's contribution really as one true art form. As we talked before, about the African....
Combination?
Rhythms and the European melodic line and harmonies, the wedding of the two has really made American jazz in my opinion. And let's hope we can keep it that way and get married for ever. (LAUGHTER).
Now of course Dave Baker is doing a good job out at Indiana University, teaching jazz.
Oh fantastic. Well I just have a feeling this is a coming thing that all the colleges and schools will eventually get to include this in their curriculum.
Well now that it's no longer in dives and no longer in sporting houses and such places (LAUGHTER) it's coming into its own, own decency huh? (LAUGHTER).
